name.text: Lines of Symmetry of a Regular polygon.

questiontext.text:
A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that are mirror images of each other. Work out the number of lines of symmetry for each regular polygon shown below.

Tip: drag the red point to rotate the dashed axis about the centre, then press Reflect. If the orange copy lands exactly on the polygon, the dashed line is a line of symmetry. Press Reset to start again.

(a)

generalfeedback.text:
A regular polygon with \(n\) sides has exactly \(n\) lines of symmetry — one for every vertex. (When \(n\) is odd each axis runs from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side; when \(n\) is even, half the axes join opposite vertices and half join the midpoints of opposite sides.)

(a) The regular \({@n1@}\)-gon has \({@ta1@}\) lines of symmetry, shown below.

[[jsxgraph height='360px' width='440px']] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 16, -2], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: { enabled: false }, zoom: { enabled: false } }); var n = {#n1#}; var cx = 7, cy = 6, r = 4; var rot = Math.random() * 360; function deg(d){ return d * Math.PI / 180; } var verts = []; for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) { var th = 90 + i * 360 / n + rot; verts.push(board.create('point', [cx + r * Math.cos(deg(th)), cy + r * Math.sin(deg(th))], { visible: false, fixed: true })); } board.create('polygon', verts, { fillColor: '#cfe2f3', fillOpacity: 0.5, borders: { strokeColor: '#000', strokeWidth: 3 }, fixed: true, vertices: { visible: false } }); var palette = ['#e41a1c','#377eb8','#4daf4a','#984ea3','#ff7f00','#a65628','#f781bf','#999999']; for (var k = 0; k < n; k++) { var a = deg(90 + k * 180 / n + rot); var A = board.create('point', [cx + r*Math.cos(a), cy + r*Math.sin(a)], { visible: false, fixed: true }); var B = board.create('point', [cx - r*Math.cos(a), cy - r*Math.sin(a)], { visible: false, fixed: true }); board.create('segment', [A, B], { strokeColor: palette[k % palette.length], strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true }); } [[/jsxgraph]]

(b) The regular \({@n2@}\)-gon has \({@ta2@}\) lines of symmetry, shown below.

[[jsxgraph height='360px' width='440px']] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 16, -2], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: { enabled: false }, zoom: { enabled: false } }); var n = {#n2#}; var cx = 7, cy = 6, r = 4; var rot = Math.random() * 360; function deg(d){ return d * Math.PI / 180; } var verts = []; for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) { var th = 90 + i * 360 / n + rot; verts.push(board.create('point', [cx + r * Math.cos(deg(th)), cy + r * Math.sin(deg(th))], { visible: false, fixed: true })); } board.create('polygon', verts, { fillColor: '#d9ead3', fillOpacity: 0.5, borders: { strokeColor: '#000', strokeWidth: 3 }, fixed: true, vertices: { visible: false } }); var palette = ['#e41a1c','#377eb8','#4daf4a','#984ea3','#ff7f00','#a65628','#f781bf','#999999']; for (var k = 0; k < n; k++) { var a = deg(90 + k * 180 / n + rot); var A = board.create('point', [cx + r*Math.cos(a), cy + r*Math.sin(a)], { visible: false, fixed: true }); var B = board.create('point', [cx - r*Math.cos(a), cy - r*Math.sin(a)], { visible: false, fixed: true }); board.create('segment', [A, B], { strokeColor: palette[k % palette.length], strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true }); } [[/jsxgraph]]

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: It looks like you have counted only one family of axes — for example just the diagonals, or just the lines through the midpoints of the sides. A regular polygon also has the other family. Use the Reflect tool to rotate the axis right around and count every position where the copy lands exactly on the shape.

falsefeedback.text: Not quite. Every line of symmetry passes through the centre. Use the Reflect tool: rotate the dashed axis and count each position where the reflected copy sits exactly on top of the polygon.
